lesson.title: Composite in Summary
lesson.summary: Understand composite in summary from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Structural Patterns
stage.subtitle: Book chapter 10
stage.description: Adapter, bridge, composite, decorator, facade, proxy, and related structures.

payload.markdown: So the Composite pattern is useful when you need to treat a collection of things in the same way as you would an individual, either because the collection is intrinsically like a component (armies and archers) or because the context gives the collection the same characteristics as the component (line items in an invoice). Composites are arranged in trees, so an operation on the whole can affect the parts, and data from the parts is transparently available via the whole. The Composite pattern makes such operations and queries transparent to the client. Trees are easy to traverse (as we shall see in the next chapter). It is easy to add new component types to Composite structures.

payload.markdown: On the downside, Composites rely on the similarity of their parts. As soon as we introduce complex rules as to which composite object can hold which set of components, our code can become hard to manage. Composites do not lend themselves well to storage in relational databases.
